subject: Insurance
title: Lapsed Policies: The Insurer's Profit
description: A 60-second lesson on Lapsed Policies: The Insurer's Profit.

hook.text: About 25% of whole life policies lapse before paying a claim. The insurer keeps all premiums paid. Pure profit.

buildup.text: People cancel policies when money gets tight, when they divorce, or when they simply forget to pay the premium.

discovery.text: Insurers factor lapse rates into pricing. They know one in four policyholders will quit.

twist.text: Some insurers are accused of making policies confusing on purpose. Complexity causes lapses. Lapses boost profits.

climax.text: A lapsed policy is the worst outcome: you paid premiums for years and your family gets nothing. Insurers win by default.

punchline.text: 25% lapse before payout. Insurers profit when you quit.

quiz.question: What percentage of whole life policies lapse before claiming?
